title: Governor of Iowa

context.text: This is an open seat: Republican Gov. Kim Reynolds is not seeking a third term. It is the first open governor's race in Iowa since 2006.

In the June 2, 2026 Republican primary, businessman and farmer Zach Lahn won the nomination with 37.65% of the vote, ahead of U.S. Rep. Randy Feenstra, who had been endorsed by President Trump. Auditor Rob Sand was the only Democrat to qualify and was unopposed.

Libertarian Nicholas Gluba and running mate Jules Cutler were removed from the ballot by the State Objection Panel in June because the panel found Cutler had not filed the required affidavit of candidacy. A Polk County District Court judge upheld the removal in late July, and the Libertarian Party of Iowa chair had said the pair was considering an appeal. They do not appear on the final certified candidate list for the general election.

candidates.name: Zach Lahn
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Derek Wulf, a state representative from the 76th district. Won the June 2 Republican primary with 37.65% of the vote.
candidates.currentRole: Farmer and businessman; co-founder of the Wonder school in Wichita, Kansas

priorities.text: Addressing what he calls a cancer crisis in Iowa by securing nitrate-free drinking water and working with farmers to reduce agricultural runoff.
priorities.quote: Iowans are just ready for something that they should be able to count on, like clean drinking water.

priorities.text: Stopping Iowa's 'brain drain' by prioritizing state incentive dollars for Iowa businesses that will stay in the state.
Banning the use of eminent domain for private gain and taxing out-of-state landowners and data centers at higher rates in order to lower property taxes.

positions.summary: A Kansas Reflector profile reports that he has opposed abortion; his specific position on Iowa's six-week ban was not found in a primary source.
The same profile reports that he has defended school vouchers.
Says he would tax out-of-state landowners and data centers at higher rates in order to lower property taxes; a Kansas Reflector profile also reports that he has opposed high taxes.

candidates.name: Rob Sand
candidates.ballotNote: Running with Lt. Gov. candidate Dave Muhlbauer, a Crawford County supervisor. Unopposed in the June 2 Democratic primary. Currently Iowa State Auditor.

priorities.text: A bipartisan approach to governing, noting he would work with the Republican-led Legislature.
priorities.quote: If I win this race, I'm going to be working with the Republican Legislature, right?

priorities.text: Ending the privatization of Iowa's Medicaid system and raising reimbursement rates for health care workers.
Addressing the state's ongoing budget deficit, which he called a "fiscal time bomb," including new revenue such as legalizing and taxing recreational cannabis products.

positions.summary: Said he disagreed with the overturning of Roe v. Wade and would veto any bill further restricting abortion access, while saying a governor cannot single-handedly repeal Iowa's six-week ban.
positions.quote: I don't make promises to people that I can't keep.

record.text: As State Auditor, released an audit report finding the Iowa Judicial Branch had sent $27.6 million in court debt collections to the wrong state fund over four years because of programming errors, shorting other state and local funds. Republican officials said his office was told of a potential problem in 2022; Sand said his office remained engaged with the judicial branch and awaited final numbers.

The Republican-led House Government Oversight Committee approved a report in February 2026 criticizing the judicial branch and Sand for not investigating the court debt issue more quickly; Sand responded that no money was lost and no services were delayed.

researchNotes: Running mates are noted in each candidate's ballotNote rather than as separate entries. Ballotpedia was not reachable (it blocks automated requests) and the Iowa Secretary of State's statewide general-election list could not be loaded. The two-candidate slate was checked against the Story County Auditor's FINAL certified general-election candidate list (which prints only Sand/Muhlbauer and Lahn/Wulf for governor), Wikipedia, and Iowa Public Radio's report that the Libertarian ticket was removed. Whether the Libertarians pursued a further appeal after the late-July district court ruling was not confirmed, but the final county list does not include them. Lahn's positions come from a news profile rather than his own materials, and a specific position on the six-week abortion ban was not found. Neither candidate has Iowa legislative votes to cite, and no cited source says whether Lahn has held elected office, so that is not stated; Sand's record items are limited to two audit-related items reported by Iowa Public Radio.
